column1: # Coverage ledger for tests/GlitchCryptoTests.cpp (GoogleTest migration; see tests/scripts/CoverageLedger.cmake).

column5: merged:GlitchCrypto.main.test_retail_digest_vectors.Call;note:its loop over the three variants is TEST_P RetailDigestVector.MatchesTheIndependentPythonVector with rows SingleCb, SplitFlags0x0800, SplitFlags0x1800 (the three Python vectors verbatim and in order, the variant formulas unchanged), bundled as bootloaders.Vector/RetailDigestVector; the 3 must() calls per variant are ASSERT_OK_AND_ASSIGN (two parses) and ASSERT_OK (encrypt_retail), and an ASSERT that the seal derived a key now guards the derived_key dereference; the 16 digest bytes are EXPECT_BYTES_EQ

merged:GlitchCrypto.main.test_retail_digest.NoSplitFlags0Change0;note:its 15 calls from the nested main() loop are TEST_P RetailDigest.CbDigestBindsTheConsoleDataAndTheSealedSmc, instantiated per regime (Single false/0, Split0800 true/0x800, Split1800 true/0x1800) over the five changes (UnchangedBigBlock 0, PairingChanged 1, CbLdvChanged 2, CpuKeyChanged 3, SmcChanged 4) through ::testing::Combine, one bundled entry per regime; the early returns are ASSERTs (build, read, parse, SMC and CB_B present, extract, rebuild); the change-3 keyvault .value() calls are ASSERT_OK_AND_ASSIGN; the digest is EXPECT_BYTES_EQ with the old split/flags/change message

merged:GlitchCrypto.main.test_build_policy.Retail;note:its ten calls are TEST_P ChainPolicy.BuildsExtractsAndRebuildsTheSealedChain, instantiated per family (Retail: Retail, RetailManufacturing; Glitch: Glitch1, Glitch2, BigBlockGlitch2; Glitch2m: Glitch2m, Glitch2mManufacturing, Glitch2mManufacturingV2; Glitch3: Glitch3, Glitch3V2), one bundled entry per family, the old name string kept as the message label; check_chain is the void helper expect_chain (ASSERTs that the image reads and parses, then one EXPECT per stage), called under EXPECT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE for the build and ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE for the rebuild; the CB_B, CD and CE && chain is one EXPECT per stage; optional stages compare through EXPECT_OPTIONAL_BYTES_EQ (presence, then bytes)
